result.reason: The passage is Rav Yosef's dilemma about rainwater and millstones (itztroblin), which is precisely what the 'Rainwater & Intent' section's prose describes and contextualizes.

The passage directly addresses the Gemara's clarification that the dilemma only applies according to the rabbanan (not Rabbi Eliezer) and concludes with teiku, which is precisely what the 'Rabbi Eliezer & Rabbis' prose section describes.

Both items together constitute the instruction from Rav Nechemiah to collect the daughter's tenth even from the itztroblin, plus Rav Ashi's related teaching about rental income — exactly what heading 3 ('The Instruction') describes, and the subsequent headings (4–8) cover the essay's prose analysis of these rulings rather than the Talmudic text itself.

Both items — the Mishnah introducing the sale of a courtyard including Rabbi Eliezer's restrictive 'airspace only' view, and the Gemara/baraita elaborating on outer/inner houses and Rabbi Eliezer's position — are precisely the content discussed in the 'Rabbi Eliezer's View' prose, which explicitly covers the baraita about outer and inner homes and Rabbi Eliezer's ruling.

The passage directly discusses stores opening into both the courtyard and public domain, the contradiction between baraitot, and the resolution based on majority use (rov tashmishta), which is precisely what the 'Courtyard Stores' prose describes.
Both items present Rabba's two versions of the linguistic analysis distinguishing dirata/darta/chatzer, which is precisely what the 'Linguistic Analysis' prose describes in detail.

All four items together constitute the complete discussion of both versions of Rav Nachman's ruling on the sand field and pond — the first version (chazaka on one does not acquire the other), the challenge from Shmuel, the distinction based on separate functions, and then the alternative version (chazaka on one does acquire the other with the reframed chidush) — which matches precisely the 'Final Resolution' prose describing the alternative version and the kamashma lan conclusion.
